title: Codex 0.157.0 no longer starts with the Arch Linux package unless --no-daemon is used

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Hi! After updating `openai-codex` from `0.156.1-1` to `0.157.0-1` with pacman on Arch Linux, just running `codex` no longer opens a usable session:

```text
Error: this CLI has no complete local package; install a packaged Codex CLI or use the standalone installer
To work without the background server, rerun the same command with --no-daemon (including resume or fork and its arguments).
```

I had recently restored a Timeshift snapshot, so at first I thought I'd broken something locally. But the same error reproduces with a fresh `CODEX_HOME`, and `pacman -Qkk openai-codex` reports `15 total files, 0 altered files`.

`codex --no-daemon` works around it. It looks related to daemon auto-start becoming the default in 0.157.0.

### Environment

- Codex: `codex-cli 0.157.0`, Arch package `openai-codex 0.157.0-1`
- OS: Arch Linux x86_64, kernel `7.2.6-zen2-1-zen`
- Terminal: Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2; also reproduced in a separate PTY without a multiplexer
- Model/subscription: the minimal reproduction below needs neither authentication nor a model request

### Reproduction

With the Arch package installed:

```sh
repro_home=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/cdx-repro.XXXXXX")
CODEX_HOME="$repro_home" /usr/bin/codex app-server daemon start
```

This exits with code 1 and the package error above. A short home path matters here because a sufficiently long one hits a separate Unix socket path-length limit.

The user-facing regression is that an ordinary interactive `codex` launch now takes this failing path by default.

### What was checked

To rule out my existing setup, these tests used separate `CODEX_HOME` directories on the same machine:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Arch 0.156.1, default interactive launch | Opens the input prompt |
| Arch 0.157.0, default interactive launch | Exits with the package error |
| Arch 0.157.0 with `--no-daemon` | Opens the input prompt |
| Arch 0.157.0 with `--disable daemon_auto_start` | Opens the input prompt |
| Arch 0.157.0, explicit daemon start | Same package error |
| Official 0.157.0 **complete package**, daemon start | Starts successfully, reports server version 0.157.0 |
| The exact same official executable copied out of that package, daemon start | Same package error |

The interactive tests used a dummy API key and a trust entry for the test directory to skip onboarding; no prompt was sent. The successful daemon was stopped after testing.

Both the complete `codex-package-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.zst` asset and the separate `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.zst` asset were checked against their GitHub SHA-256 digests. The standalone binary decompresses to exactly the same executable used in the last test.

### Possible cause

The [Arch PKGBUILD](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/openai-codex/-/blob/0.157.0-1/PKGBUILD) installs the executables into `/usr/bin` and uses system dependencies. It doesn't install `codex-package.json` or the bundled `codex-path` / `codex-resources` layout that the official complete package has.

Looking at the tagged source:

- `daemon_auto_start` changed from [default false in 0.156.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L937) to [default true in 0.157.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L940).
- [Package detection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/install-context/src/lib.rs#L286) needs `codex-package.json` next to the `bin` directory.
- [Daemon installation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/prepare_install.rs#L146) returns this error when there is no recognized source package and no existing daemon installation to use.

I'm not sure how much of this should be fixed upstream versus in Arch's packaging. Could automatic startup fall back to the embedded server when the complete package layout isn't available? Explicitly starting the daemon could still report the missing requirements. If downstream packages need a new layout, some guidance for packagers would also help.

For now, this gets normal interactive use working again:

```sh
codex features disable daemon_auto_start
```

Thanks for taking a look. I found #47990 while searching, but that seems to be an npm dependency publishing issue rather than this native package startup failure.

### Codex doctor report

The relevant part of `codex doctor --json` from an isolated, credential-free home is below. Interestingly, the install check passes. Other checks are omitted here; missing authentication in that environment is intentional.

```json
{
  "codexVersion": "0.157.0",
  "installation": {
    "status": "ok",
    "summary": "installation looks consistent",
    "details": {
      "current executable": "/usr/bin/codex",
      "install context": "other",
      "managed package root": "not set"
    }
  }
}
```
